nodes.content: Characterize sharp policy-value bounds for clinical decision policies with selectively observed outcomes and bounded unmeasured confounding.
requirements: Specify sensitivity assumptions and characterize when bounds certify improvement over the historical policy.
Achieve at least 95% confidence-set coverage uniformly over the stated sensitivity model.

nodes.content: Optimize policy-minus-historical value over latent-outcome tables with Γ-bounded assignment and recording odds ratios; project exact 95% multinomial confidence regions.
Does optimizing policy and historical values separately destroy sharpness of improvement bounds under shared latent confounding?
Joint optimization gives sharp improvement bounds, sometimes strictly tighter than subtracting separate marginal intervals under shared latent confounding.
Derive joint Γ-constrained latent-table extrema, compare marginal subtraction, and certify improvement when the projected exact-95% lower bound exceeds zero.
Implement and benchmark joint versus marginal Γ-constrained extrema with exact-95% projection on two-stratum treatment-outcome-recording tables.
ΓTable v0.1 packages a two-stratum latent-table solver, marginal-subtraction comparator, and exact-95% multinomial confidence-region projection scripts.
Use ΓTable v0.1 on two-stratum Γ=2 scenarios to compare joint and marginal bound widths and audit exact-95% coverage.
Across 400 Γ=2 tables, mean joint width was 0.12 versus 0.19 marginally; minimum simulated coverage was 95.1%.
Using ΓTable v0.1, search 500 Γ=2 two-stratum tables for attainable joint extrema and strictly loose marginal-subtraction bounds.
In 7/500 Γ=2 tables, joint lower bounds undershot certified attainable extrema by 0.03, exposing incompatible assignment-recording confounder mixtures.
Enforcing a shared confounder mixture across assignment and recording closes the 0.03 unattainability gap and restores sharp joint bounds.
Replace separate odds-ratio relaxations with shared-mixture latent cells, prove attainable extrema, and retest exact-95% projection against marginal subtraction.
Implement shared-mixture latent-cell constraints in ΓTable v0.2 and rerun the seven Γ=2 counterexamples with attainable-extremum certificates.
ΓTable v0.2 contains shared-confounder mixture constraints, attainable-extremum certificate generation, and exact-95% confidence-region projection.
Use ΓTable v0.2 to certify extrema for seven counterexamples and verify uniform 95% coverage via multinomial test inversion.
ΓTable v0.2 closed all seven Γ=2 unattainability gaps below 10⁻⁶; exact multinomial inversion guarantees at least 95% coverage uniformly.
Stress-test ΓTable v0.2 across Γ∈{1,2,3} continuous-confounder models, comparing certified bounds with independently discretized attainable-value searches.
At Γ=3, certified continuous-confounder optimization gave a sharp lower bound of −0.05; ΓTable v0.2 returned −0.08.
Extremal continuous confounder distributions admit finite atomic representations with coupled assignment-recording moments, closing the Γ=3 gap.
Derive finite-atomic extrema under coupled Γ-odds constraints; compare joint improvement bounds with marginal subtraction using exact-95% projection.
Extend ΓTable v0.2 with finite-atomic coupled-moment optimization and retest the Γ=3 lower bound against −0.05.
ΓTable v0.3 replaces v0.2’s fixed latent cells with adaptive finite-atomic optimization enforcing coupled assignment-recording moments.
Check whether ΓTable v0.3 closes the Γ=3 −0.08-to−0.05 gap using continuous-confounder dual certificates and exact-95% projection.
ΓTable v0.3’s six-atom solution attained −0.0500 at Γ=3, matching the continuous-confounder dual bound within 10⁻⁶.
Adopt v0.3’s joint bounds for exact-95% improvement certification above zero; v0.2 passed discrete checks but missed continuous-confounder extrema.
Use binary-outcome linear-fractional programming with Γ treatment and Λ recording odds; invert exact multinomial tests to certify positive policy gains.
Can linear-fractional extrema remain sharp when treatment and recording share an unrestricted confounder under separate Γ and Λ bounds?
Finite atomic support plus coupled treatment-recording constraints makes Γ–Λ linear-fractional improvement extrema attainable for binary outcomes.
Benchmark coupled Γ–Λ finite-atom bounds against continuous-confounder dual certificates across 300 binary-outcome tables; verify exact-95% test inversion.
At Γ=2, Λ=3, 11/300 finite-atom lower bounds exceeded attainable minima by 0.02; worst-case empirical coverage was 93.7%.
Reject the Γ–Λ linear-fractional proposal: 0.02 sharpness failures and 93.7% worst-case coverage violate both requirements.
Use infinite-dimensional moment optimization under coupled Γ/Λ odds constraints; project exact multinomial confidence regions onto sharp improvement bounds.
Can coupled Γ/Λ moment duals certify attainable extrema without the finite-atom approximation that caused 0.02 sharpness errors?
Prove coupled Γ/Λ moment duality, construct attaining extremizers, and retest eleven failures with exact-95% multinomial inversion.
Implement adaptive column generation with Γ/Λ moment dual certificates; rerun eleven failed tables and audit exact multinomial inversion.
MomentPolicy v1.0 contains a coupled Γ/Λ column-generation solver, primal-dual sharpness certificates, and exact multinomial inversion scripts.
Run MomentPolicy v1.0 primal-dual certificates on eleven Γ=2, Λ=3 failures; audit exact-95% inversion across 300 tables.
MomentPolicy v1.0 closed all eleven primal-dual gaps below 10⁻⁶; exact test inversion guarantees at least 95% uniform coverage.
Use conditional total-variation budgets for treatment confounding and selective recording; optimize joint binary response types with exact multinomial inversion.
Do separate conditional total-variation budgets permit sharp policy-gain bounds when treatment assignment and outcome recording share latent response types?
A single response-type distribution satisfying both conditional TV budgets yields attainable joint gain extrema, unlike independently optimized margins.
Extend MomentPolicy v1.0 with TV-constrained response-type optimization; benchmark primal-dual sharpness against independent margins and exact-95% coverage.
Across 200 binary tables at TV budgets 0.10/0.15, joint gains had certified 10⁻⁶ dual gaps and 18% narrower intervals.
Use ΓTable v0.3 to audit TV-budget response-type bounds against continuous-confounder extrema and exact-95% coverage across 500 tables.
At TV budgets 0.10/0.15, 9/500 TV-compliant continuous-confounder tables breached joint lower bounds by 0.015; minimum coverage was 94.2%.
Audit nine TV-budget breaches using ΓTable v0.3 and MomentPolicy v1.0, testing whether conditioning on recording breaks shared-type feasibility.
Correcting recording-conditioned TV implementation eliminated nine breaches, matched extrema within 10⁻⁶, and restored exact-test 95% coverage.
Retain corrected TV bounds: 18% narrower, nine breaches resolved; certify improvement when the projected exact-95% gain lower bound exceeds zero.
Optimize joint policy-gain bounds under shared-latent KL budgets of 0.05 nats for assignment and recording; certify positive exact-95% lower bounds.
Can shared-latent KL constraints yield attainable gain extrema when outcome recording depends on unobserved potential outcomes?
A shared response-type distribution satisfying both 0.05-nat KL budgets attains gain extrema despite outcome-dependent recording.
Derive shared-latent KL primal-dual bounds, construct attaining response-type distributions, and project exact-95% multinomial confidence regions.
Implement KL-constrained shared-type optimization at 0.05 nats; compare primal-dual certificates with exact-95% projections on 200 outcome-dependent-recording tables.
KLPolicy v0.1 includes a shared-response-type KL optimizer, primal-dual certificates, and exact-95% multinomial projection scripts.
Run KLPolicy v0.1 on 200 outcome-dependent-recording tables at 0.05 nats, auditing primal-dual attainability and exact-95% projection coverage.
Across 200 tables, feasible KLPolicy v0.1 extremizers matched duals within 10⁻⁶; exact inversion guarantees ≥95% uniform coverage.
Stress-test KLPolicy v0.1 on continuous-confounder models with 1% outcome recording, checking extremal attainability and exact-95% coverage.
At 1% recording, feasible shared-type gains approached −0.12 but never attained it; extremizing sequences had vanishing recording propensities.
At 0.05 nats, sharp gain infima need not be attained; requiring recording propensity ≥0.005 restores attainment.
Add recording-propensity floor 0.005, prove compactness and extremizer existence, then rerun sparse-recording coverage tests.
Modify KLPolicy v0.1 to enforce recording propensities ≥0.005; test extremizer attainment and exact-95% coverage on 1%-recording tables.
KLPolicy v0.2 adds a 0.005 recording-propensity floor and compactness-based extremizer certificates to v0.1’s KL optimization.
Test KLPolicy v0.2 on 1%-recording models for attained extrema, primal-dual gaps below 10⁻⁶, and exact-95% coverage.
In 120/200 sparse-recording tables, floor-inactive extremizers matched unrestricted KL duals within 10⁻⁶; exact-test coverage remained ≥95%.
Stress-test KLPolicy v0.2 on floor-active 1%-recording tables, checking extremizer certificates and exact-95% coverage under the 0.005 floor.
In 4/80 tables, certified −0.11 gain infima were unattained as treatment propensities vanished despite the 0.005 recording floor.
Add a 0.005 treatment-propensity floor to KLPolicy v0.2; retest four unattained −0.11 infima for attainment and exact-95% coverage.
Rechecking four −0.11 cases revealed faulty vanishing-treatment certificates: recording floor alone attained extrema; added 0.005 treatment floor was inactive.
Adopt KLPolicy v0.2’s recording floor; reject the unnecessary treatment floor after corrected certificates restore attainment and exact-95% coverage.
Retain KLPolicy v0.2 with the 0.005 recording floor: it restores attainable sharp bounds and exact-95% improvement certification.
Select ΓTable v0.3, MomentPolicy v1.0, corrected TV, and KLPolicy v0.2; reject finite-atom shortcuts; certify positive exact-95% lower bounds.
